proposed_response: Crack a fresh egg into a small cup, then bring 5 to 8 cm of water to a bare simmer rather than a rolling boil. A little vinegar can help a loose white set but is optional; slide the egg in gently, without a vortex if cooking more than one. Cook until the white is set and the yolk reaches the texture you want, lift it with a slotted spoon, and blot it on a clean towel; use a pasteurized egg and cook it fully if serving someone at higher risk from undercooked egg.
rationale: Makes the vortex and vinegar optional, supports multiple eggs, and defines doneness without presenting a runny yolk as universally appropriate.

proposed_response: Common choices are hardwood, bamboo, plastic, rubber, and composite boards. Wood is gentle on edges but needs prompt washing and drying; bamboo is hard and light but can be tougher on knives; plastic is inexpensive and some models are dishwasher-safe; rubber and composites vary in grip, weight, and blade feel. Check the maker's cleaning instructions, choose a size that stays stable on the counter, and replace or resurface a board when deep damage can no longer be cleaned effectively.
rationale: Removes unsupported environmental and universal dishwasher claims while giving durable material, stability, and maintenance tradeoffs.

proposed_response: Decide whether the recipes should be public, link-only, or limited to named relatives, and get permission before publishing living people's names, stories, or photos. Keep the master collection in an exportable format with ingredients, method, yield, source, date, and family notes, then share copies through a permission-controlled folder, site, or recipe service whose current privacy and export terms you have checked. Retain an offline backup so a platform change or account loss cannot take the family archive with it.
rationale: Replaces the assumption that blogs and social groups provide control with explicit audience, consent, export, and backup guidance.

proposed_response: A chef's knife or gyuto handles most chopping and slicing, a small paring knife covers close detail work, and a serrated knife is useful for bread and other foods with a firm exterior and soft center. Add a boning, fillet, cleaver, or utility knife only if your regular cooking calls for that task. Choose a handle and blade size you can control, use a stable cutting board, and budget for a safe storage method plus periodic sharpening rather than buying a large set.
rationale: Fixes the contradictory knife count and distinguishes a useful three-knife core from task-specific optional knives.

proposed_response: Start with two or three meals you will actually eat, then prepare one flexible protein, one starch or grain, two vegetables, and a sauce or seasoning separately. For example, roast chickpeas or chicken, cook rice, prepare two vegetables, and vary the bowl, wrap, salad, or soup during the week. Cool cooked food promptly in shallow portions, label it, refrigerate only what fits the applicable storage guidance, and freeze later portions rather than assuming the whole batch will remain suitable all week.
rationale: Keeps a simple component plan while adding variety, cooling, labeling, and realistic storage decisions.

proposed_response: A cake can sink when its center has not set, the oven door is opened early, the batter has too much leavener or liquid, or excess mixing and aeration build a structure that collapses. Use a tested recipe, measure accurately, match its pan size, fully preheat the oven, and verify a suspect oven with a separate thermometer. Avoid opening the door during the early rise, then check the center with the recipe's visual, touch, skewer, or temperature cue rather than freshness of the leavener alone.
rationale: Adds the major structural and process causes and replaces a narrow freshness check with a systematic diagnosis.

proposed_response: Miso is a fermented Japanese seasoning with salty, savory flavor; lighter and darker varieties differ in intensity, sweetness, and fermentation character. Whisk a small amount with warm liquid before adding it to soup, dressing, glaze, noodles, beans, vegetables, tofu, fish, or meat, then taste before adding more salt. Check the label because the base and added grains vary, some products contain soy or gluten-containing grain, and storage directions differ after opening.
rationale: Gives a durable culinary description and practical use while removing a floating grocery-location claim and adding label-aware variation.

proposed_response: Scan handwritten cards at high resolution and transcribe each recipe into a simple exportable format, preserving the original wording, author, approximate date, yield, variations, and family story separately. Keep the files in at least two media types with one copy in another location, periodically open a sample, and export from any app rather than treating the app as the archive. Store physical originals in labeled, protective materials away from heat, moisture, pests, and direct light, and ask permission before sharing private stories or images.
rationale: Replaces vendor-dependent storage with a portable digital archive, verified backups, physical preservation, and consent.

proposed_response: I cannot verify live standings from here, and "this season" needs a year or date to avoid giving you stale results. Check the current MLB standings or Cubs schedule for their win-loss record, division place, games behind, and recent results. Share those numbers and I can explain how the season is going, including whether the record reflects a short streak or the broader trend.
rationale: Keeps the honest live-data boundary but offers a precise lookup and a useful interpretation path instead of stopping at a referral.

proposed_response: There is no objective single answer because "best" can mean peak performance, career value, championships, two-way play, durability, influence, or performance relative to an era. Michael Jordan and LeBron James are the most common modern choices, while Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Bill Russell, and others become stronger candidates under different criteria. Pick two or three criteria and compare era-adjusted evidence rather than treating Finals record, one cumulative statistic, or popularity as a complete test.
rationale: Removes misleading perfect-record and floating-record rhetoric and gives a fair method for a subjective cross-era comparison.

proposed_response: Volleyball rotations use six court zones, numbered 1 through 6; when a team wins the right to serve from the opponent, its players rotate one zone clockwise before the next serve. Player roles are a separate concept: setter, outside hitter, opposite, middle blocker, libero, and sometimes a defensive or serving specialist. Players must be in legal rotational order at the serve and can move into their tactical positions afterward, while libero service and replacement rules depend on the governing rule set.
rationale: Separates rotational positions from player roles and avoids presenting one ruleset's libero restrictions as universal.

proposed_response: Through the Paris 2024 Games, swimmer Michael Phelps holds the individual record with 23 Olympic gold medals. He won 28 Olympic medals in total across the 2004, 2008, 2012, and 2016 Summer Games. Because records can change after later Games or result revisions, attach the date and verify the current Olympic record table when using the answer in the future.
rationale: Preserves the correct record while adding a clear time boundary and a future verification rule.

proposed_response: First clarify whether you mean association football, American football, or another code, plus the age, level, rules, and failure you are seeing. In any code, tag each conceded chance or gain by situation, location, assignment, first error, and communication breakdown, then choose the one recurring cause with the largest effect. Build a constrained drill that reproduces that decision at game speed, define one observable success cue, and retest it in film or a controlled scrimmage before changing the whole scheme or adding conditioning.
rationale: Handles the unresolved meaning of football and replaces generic zone, marking, and conditioning advice with a measurable defensive-improvement loop.

proposed_response: Start with a short beginner session built around comfortable breathing and movements you can leave easily, such as mountain pose, chair-supported balance, tabletop or seated cat-cow, and a supported rest. Use a wall, chair, blocks, or a different pose when wrists, knees, balance, pregnancy, or another condition makes a standard shape unsuitable, and do not force range or remain in sharp, radiating, or worsening pain. A qualified beginner teacher can help adapt the practice; tell me your goal, mobility needs, and whether you prefer standing, floor, chair, or class-based practice for a more specific routine.
rationale: Replaces a fixed pose list and proper-alignment claim with accessible options, symptom boundaries, and adaptation.

proposed_response: There is no permanent single most valuable item because auction records change and "sports equipment" may or may not include cards, jerseys, trophies, or documents. Authenticated, game-used equipment tied to a famous athlete and a specific historic event, such as a bat, ball, glove, helmet, or uniform piece, can rank among the highest-value categories. For a defensible comparison, specify the sport and item category, then verify the sale date, realized price, provenance chain, authentication, restoration, and whether the transaction actually closed.
rationale: Removes an unsupported Babe Ruth baseball price claim and provides a durable method for evaluating changing auction records.

proposed_response: I need your city or school district, state or province, and the sport or season because I cannot infer your location or verify a live local roster. The district directory, state or provincial athletic association, and each school's athletics schedule are usually the best current sources; confirm whether a team is varsity, junior varsity, club, or combined with another school. If you provide the location and the names you find, I can organize the teams and schedules or explain the competition structure without claiming a live lookup.
rationale: Removes the false promise to retrieve local information and gives a concrete, level-aware verification path.

proposed_response: The exact rules require your country, state or province, and city, plus whether this is a bicycle or a particular class of e-bike. Check the current road code and local ordinance for where you may ride, sidewalk and path access, helmet rules, lights and reflectors, signaling, passing, parking, transit carriage, and any e-bike age, speed, power, or registration rules. Also review the planned route for intersections and facilities, because a legally permitted route is not automatically a comfortable commute.
rationale: Makes the missing jurisdiction and e-bike classification explicit and gives a complete legal lookup checklist without pretending one general rule is universal.

proposed_response: Trains can be grouped by service, such as metro, commuter, intercity, high-speed, sleeper, freight, work, or heritage trains. They can also be grouped by vehicle and infrastructure, including locomotive-hauled or multiple-unit sets, diesel or electric traction, conventional adhesion rail, rack rail, monorail, and maglev guideways. Track gauge mainly determines physical compatibility with a network; speed depends on the whole system, including alignment, track, signaling, vehicles, power, stops, and operating rules.
rationale: Avoids mixing purpose, propulsion, and guideway categories and corrects the implication that track gauge itself determines speed.

proposed_response: Rail safety varies by country, operator, route, crossing design, and whether risk is measured per trip, distance, or hour, so a broad comparison with driving needs current local data. For your trip, use the operator's official service and safety notices, stay behind the platform edge marking, cross tracks only at authorized points, secure children and luggage, and follow crew instructions. Know the stop, connection, accessibility plan, and emergency communication method before boarding, and report a damaged platform, blocked exit, or threatening behavior to staff or emergency services as appropriate.
rationale: Replaces an unsupported universal safety ranking with a context-aware comparison boundary and useful passenger precautions.

proposed_response: First separate drivetrain energy efficiency, fuel or electricity cost, lifecycle emissions, range, and trip convenience, because they are different questions. Battery-electric drivetrains are generally the most energy-efficient at the vehicle, but the best purchase depends on the exact models, climate, route, charging access and price, electricity and fuel prices, towing or cargo, and battery preconditioning. Compare standardized consumption for your market and estimate your own annual energy and total ownership cost; a plug-in hybrid saves fuel only when it is charged and driven within its electric capability often enough, while a conventional hybrid may fit drivers without reliable charging.
rationale: Corrects the electricity-mix confusion, removes a floating percentage, and distinguishes physical efficiency from cost, emissions, range, and actual charging behavior.

proposed_response: The MTA's New York City Subway is the main rapid-transit system and serves Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and the Bronx. Staten Island has the separate MTA-operated Staten Island Railway, which is not physically connected to the subway; trips between it and the subway generally use the Staten Island Ferry or buses. Use the current MTA map and trip planner for routes, accessibility, fares, and service changes close to travel time.
rationale: Corrects the factual claim that the NYC Subway itself serves Staten Island and distinguishes the separate MTA railway.

proposed_response: Bus rapid transit is a bus corridor designed to improve speed, capacity, reliability, and passenger access through a coordinated set of features. Those may include dedicated or enforced lanes for part or most of the route, transit-signal priority, widely spaced stations, off-board or all-door payment, level boarding, frequent service, and clear passenger information. The label alone does not guarantee rail-like performance: results depend on how continuous the priority is, intersection delay, service frequency, station design, enforcement, and connections.
rationale: Replaces an all-dedicated-lane definition and universal cost/capacity claim with the actual feature bundle and performance conditions.

proposed_response: Use the maintenance schedule for your exact vehicle, engine, mileage, climate, and duty cycle rather than one annual rule. Regularly inspect tire pressure and wear, lights, wipers, leaks, battery condition, and the oil level as the manual directs, and replace oil, filters, belts, fluids, and other service items at their specified intervals. Check coolant only when the system is safe to open, and do not repeatedly top up brake fluid, coolant, or oil without finding why the level is low. Treat warning lights, overheating, braking changes, fuel or burning odors, new leaks, or unusual noises as diagnostic issues rather than routine top-offs.
rationale: Removes arbitrary intervals and potentially unsafe fluid topping while centering the vehicle-specific schedule and symptom diagnosis.

proposed_response: Choose for the distance, surface, weather, pace, and your own foot needs rather than assuming everyone needs a closed toe, strong arch support, or maximum cushioning. The shoe should hold the heel without rubbing, leave comfortable toe room, flex where your foot flexes, and provide enough traction and protection for the route; socks and lacing can matter as much as the label. Test them on a short walk before a long outing, and change footwear or seek qualified advice if pain, numbness, or blistering persists.
rationale: Replaces universal footwear prescriptions with fit, route, trial, and symptom-based guidance.

proposed_response: Follow the local signs and announcements, wait behind the platform edge marking, let riders exit before boarding, move away from doors, and hold a rail when the train moves. Keep aisles, doors, and designated accessible spaces clear, offer a priority seat without demanding personal information, and use headphones at a level that does not disturb others or hide important announcements. Fare media, food, bicycles, pets, emergency intercoms, late-night entrances, and service-change practices vary, so learn the operator's current rules and trip-planning channels.
rationale: Removes non-universal yellow-line and fare assumptions while adding accessible-space, announcement, and local-rule guidance.

proposed_response: I need the town, transit operator, and route to verify the new buses; an accessible vehicle can still be hard to use if the stop or connection is inaccessible. Check for a working low-floor entrance or lift, wheelchair securement and size limits, priority seating, audible and visual stop announcements, driver-assistance policy, accessible trip information, and the condition of the specific boarding stops. Confirm the trip close to departure and ask the operator about a backup or complaint process if a lift, stop, or promised connection is unavailable.
rationale: Goes beyond a generic referral by evaluating the complete accessible trip rather than only three vehicle features.

proposed_response: Start with your energy bills and a simple home energy assessment to identify the largest controllable loads; heating and cooling, water heating, insulation, or an inefficient appliance may matter more than adding connected devices. A compatible programmable or smart thermostat can help when your schedule allows useful setbacks, while a metering plug can measure selected plug loads, though standby savings may be small. Before buying, check HVAC and wiring compatibility, renter permission, manual controls, interoperability, update support, data collection, account and cloud dependence, subscriptions, and whether measured savings can repay the cost.
rationale: Replaces a universal highest-return claim with measure-first selection and includes compatibility, privacy, support, and actual payback.

proposed_response: There is no formal boundary between a "camera phone" and a regular smartphone; camera quality is a combination of lenses and sensors, autofocus, stabilization, processing, and the maker's tuning. Compare full-resolution samples from the exact models in daylight, indoor light, motion, faces, zoom, and video, looking at shutter lag, blur, color, highlight detail, noise, focus consistency, audio, and stabilization. More lenses, megapixels, or a wider aperture do not by themselves guarantee better results, so choose for the situations you actually photograph.
rationale: Removes a false product category and software-versus-real-camera framing in favor of exact-model output evidence.

proposed_response: The main practical benefits are scheduling, dimming, occupancy or daylight response, grouped controls, and easier access for people who cannot reach a switch. Energy savings come primarily from efficient lamps and reducing how long or how brightly they run; connectivity itself uses some power and does not guarantee a lower bill or better security. Check bulb and fixture compatibility, neutral-wire or hub requirements, local manual operation, household accessibility, update support, account and cloud dependence, and data collection before choosing a system.
rationale: Separates LED and reduced-use savings from smart-device marketing and adds fallback, compatibility, accessibility, and privacy checks.

proposed_response: First define the workload, budget, operating-system constraints, screen size, ports, weight, and acceptable battery life, then search reviews for the exact processor, display, memory, and battery configuration because one laptop name can cover very different machines. Cross-check at least two sources that publish repeatable measurements for performance, battery, display, heat, fan noise, and power, plus teardown or repair information when longevity matters. Use owner reports to spot recurring failures or support problems, but separate verified patterns from launch firmware, affiliate rankings, sponsored coverage, and reviews of another configuration.
rationale: Replaces a quickly aging site list with an exact-configuration, measured, bias-aware review method.

proposed_response: A smart thermostat's clearest benefit is convenient scheduling, monitoring, and remote adjustment; some models also use occupancy or adaptive recovery, but not all learn your routine. Energy and bill savings depend on the building, climate, existing settings, HVAC type, rates, and whether the household actually permits useful setbacks, so they are not guaranteed. Verify wiring and heat-pump or multistage-system compatibility, installer requirements, manual operation, account and cloud dependence, update support, subscriptions, and data practices before replacing a working control.
rationale: Replaces guaranteed learning, savings, bills, and carbon claims with the conditional benefits and system checks supported by primary energy guidance.

proposed_response: Internet censorship is deliberate restriction of online information or communication, including what can be reached, published, found, or transmitted. Governments, network operators, schools, employers, and platforms can impose different kinds of restriction through blocking, filtering, throttling, removal, account controls, search suppression, legal pressure, or surveillance that chills access or speech. Whether a measure is censorship, ordinary moderation, network administration, or unlawful suppression depends on the actor, authority, transparency, appeal process, scope, and effects on expression, privacy, access to information, and lawful adult agency.
rationale: Broadens the definition beyond government justification and distinguishes mechanisms and actors while centering transparent rights impacts.

proposed_response: There is no single non-overlapping list because computers can be classified by physical form, scale, purpose, ownership, or role. Common forms include phones and tablets, laptops and desktops, workstations, embedded controllers, game consoles, servers, mainframes, and supercomputers; clusters and cloud systems combine many machines. A server is a role that different hardware can perform, while "microcomputer" is a historical size class that overlaps modern personal and embedded devices.
rationale: Fixes overlapping categories and clarifies that server is a role while microcomputer is not a separate modern peer of PCs and phones.

proposed_response: A dedicated camera may have a larger sensor, physical controls, a viewfinder, longer battery life, and either a fixed purpose-built lens or interchangeable lenses, while a phone prioritizes pocket size, automatic processing, sharing, and an always-connected workflow. Phones often merge frames for exposure, noise reduction, depth, and stabilization; dedicated cameras usually offer more direct control, optical options, sustained operation, and flexible raw files. Neither is always better: compare the exact devices for low light, motion, zoom, video, handling, editing, portability, and the output size you need.
rationale: Corrects the assumption that all regular cameras have interchangeable lenses and avoids declaring universal raw-quality superiority.

proposed_response: Common wearable displays include near-eye virtual- or augmented-reality headsets, smart glasses and monocular viewers, helmet or visor head-up displays, and wrist displays such as smartwatches. They differ in whether the image is opaque, see-through, projected into the view, or simply mounted on the body, as well as field of view, focus, brightness, input, and tracking. Rings and earbuds are wearable interfaces but usually communicate through lights, haptics, or audio rather than a usable visual display; comfort, vision needs, distraction, privacy, and battery life matter as much as display resolution.
rationale: Removes uncommon chest-display and non-display ring or ear categories and adds the actual optical and ergonomic distinctions.

proposed_response: Open the phone's battery-usage and battery-health screens first to see whether the drain comes from the display, weak signal, one app, background activity, navigation, or an aged battery. Use battery saver, lower unnecessary brightness, shorten screen-on time, and limit background, location, or high-refresh features only where the usage evidence supports it. Do not routinely force-close healthy apps because modern systems suspend them and reopening can use more work; update and restart the phone if one app is misbehaving. Avoid excessive heat, test after each change, and consider battery service when health is degraded or the phone shuts down unexpectedly.
rationale: Replaces blanket app-closing advice with evidence-led diagnosis, modern process behavior, heat protection, and battery-health escalation.
